acquisition_channels.details: Initial samples went to friends and family; the founders also sought word of mouth and early reviews.
Eli manually messaged Instagram influencers, often those with fewer than 10,000 followers, offering free coffee and asking them to post if they liked it.
Organic influencer posts and affiliate content; Instagram was used, and TikTok was tried briefly.
Meta/Facebook ads were the strongest reported acquisition channel; Google Ads were added later.
Amazon launch was planned, with inventory and advertising to follow after reviews.
Eli called retail buyers introduced through distributors.
Distributor relationships opened retail accounts; influencer affiliate partnerships also generated sales.
The founders sometimes ran tastings and demos at stores.

ideas.delivery: A local manufacturer roasts, blends, packs and fulfills the coffee. Mccor sells one-off and subscription orders through its online store and through retail distributors; Eli and his partner handle business development and customer service, with an offshore contractor posting on Instagram.

prices: $22–$30 per bag, depending on subscription quantity
$30.95 whole bean and $32.95 ground (host read from site)
About $23–$24 per bag for a two-bag order
$45 per pound for chaga ingredient cost
About $10 for bundle app; about $100/month plus 1% fee for Loop

uk_legal_risk.reason: The founders used unsolicited Instagram DMs to individual influencers as a meaningful customer-acquisition tactic. In the UK, unsolicited direct marketing by social DM to individuals is restricted under PECR; cold calls to business buyers also need TPS/CTPS screening.

ideas.other_uk_rules: For a UK launch, check food safety, ingredient/allergen labelling and rules on nutrition and health claims, especially the anti-inflammatory positioning. UK GDPR and PECR apply to customer data and email/SMS marketing. Consumer subscription terms and cancellation requirements under the DMCC Act may also apply.
